items.originalTitle: Microsoft’s Outlook outage didn’t end when it was fixed — a backlog of retried emails can take hours to days to clear
items.originalSummary: At 9AM last Thursday, everything seemed normal. Microsoft employees were arriving on campus, ready for a regular day of emails and meetings. But barely an hour later, one of Microsoft’s worst outages in history started to unfold, leaving employees, businesses, and many governments without access to Outlook emails for nearly 24 hours. It all started in Switzerland, according to a source familiar with the outage. Exchange Online servers that power Outlook started to fall offline. The problem quickly spread to Mexico, and then to other countries around the world, as Microsoft’s failover systems tried to shift email traffic elsewhere. Within a couple of hours, more than 80 percent of Exchange servers were unresponsive. Sources tell me that Microsoft marked the outage as “sev0” in its internal incident tracking system, the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Hundreds of engineers began trying to figure out what had gone wrong, and how to restore service. It’s not unusual for servers to fail under certain circumstances, but Microsoft has a variety of systems that are supposed to route traffic toward healthy servers to keep the broader system online. In this case, the failover systems did their job, but they also spread the problem. In the early hours of the outage, engineers were analyzing crash reports, trace logs, and kernel dumps to try and find clues to the giant outage. Some servers had entered into maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads. Engineers tried to bring servers back online, but they were almost immediately overwhelmed by traffic waiting to access the servers. Exchange servers boot up and run an OS over a network (Preboot Execution Environment), a process that allows Microsoft’s support staff and engineers to manage OS updates remotely. I understand that the sudden burst of traffic from servers being rebooted was overwhelming the systems monitoring them, causing a form of reboot loop where they kept trying and failing to come back online. As engineers continued to hunt for the root cause, Microsoft was even struggling to roll back servers to a healthy state using its usual processes of reverting recent changes. As the outside world began to wonder if this outage was related to a cyberattack or sloppy AI coding, Microsoft’s engineers were already investigating potential attack vectors and liaising with DDoS specialists to understand whether this could have been an attack. I’m told crash reports and logs quickly ruled out the possibility of an attack, and after recent rollbacks failed, Microsoft’s engineers began to take a closer look at the networking stack of the servers and discovered an unusual bug. It was unusual because the bug had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers. “A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions,” wrote Charles Lamanna, the leader of Microsoft’s Copilot, Agents, and Platform (CAP) team, in a post on X. Great Deals on Outdoor Apparel REI Co-Op 650 Down Jacket for $97 ($32 off) The 650 Down Jacket is one of the best budget three-season puffer jackets you can buy, more so at this price. At 10.9 ounces, it's reasonably lightweight and has large hand pockets and some very nice internal pockets for stashing a hat or gloves. The kids' version is also on sale in a nice yellow color that's handy for spotting your child in the snow. Mountain Hardwear Ghost Whisperer Down Jacket for $245 ($105 off) The Ghost Whisperer Down Jacket is my top pick for a backpacking puffer jacket. It weighs just 6.7 ounces for a men's medium (7.3 ounces for the men's large I tested), packs down to a tiny little thing (stuffing into its own pocket), and the 1,000-fill-power goose down offers one of the best warmth-to-weight ratios on the market. The men's version is technically on sale right now, but the only size available is small and XXL. Rab Mythic G Jacket for $440 ($90 off) This is my favorite puffer jacket, especially in the shoulder seasons when temps dip a little lower. It features 4.5 ounces of 1,000-fill down (men’s medium), which is half the weight of the overall jacket. The internal TILT lining (short for Thermo Ionic Lining Technology) may or may not do anything; I haven't been able to devise an effective test, but even if it did nothing, the amount of 1,000-fill-power down combined with the scant weight makes this an appealing option for ultralighters. The 7D fabric (which is what keeps the weight low) does need babying, but I haven't had any issues in over a year of use. REI Co-Op Campwell Down Parka for $179 ($60 off) This is great deal on a very warm down parka. It's thigh-length, which helps keep drafts up your back to a minimum, and it fits pretty well, though it's definitely boxy (what do you want from a 650-down-fill parka that's designed primarily to keep you warm?). I did find that the main two-way zipper can be fiddly, and does sometimes snag, but it's hardly a deal-breaker, especially at this price. Deals on Tents Six Moon Designs Lunar Solo Backpacking Tent for $195 ($65 off) Six Moon Design's Lunar Solo is one of the best single-wall ultralight solo tents you can buy. It's not without its quirks (read the pitching tips), but if you want something more than a tarp, that still weighs just 26 ounces (740 grams), this one is hard to beat. Use the Code YULEHIKE to get the 25 percent off. Nemo Hornet Osmo 1-Person Tent for $345 ($115 off) Nemo's Hornet tents are some of the lightest freestanding tents around. The 1-person model is my go-to for situations where I might have to pitch on rock or concrete slabs (like staying in towns on a longer bikepacking trip). It's roomy enough for you and all your gear, light enough at 2.25 pounds (without stakes), and packs down remarkably small. historyItems.originalTitle: The first Nvidia RTX Spark mini PCs launch today from Asus, Dell, and MSI
historyItems.originalSummary: After the first RTX Spark laptops launched earlier this year, Nvidia’s RTX Spark N1X chip is also now available in desktops from Asus, Dell, and MSI . More RTX Spark desktops are coming later from Acer, Gigabyte, and HP, while Microsoft’s Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is slated to start shipping this month. The new mini PCs include a 6144-core Nvidia Blackwell RTX GPU, 20-core Nvidia Grace CPU, and up to 128GB of memory. That high-end hardware comes with a price to match — Asus’s ProArt GR1X starts at $4,499 for a configuration with 64GB of memory and 1TB of storage. Like the RTX Spark laptops that compete with the MacBook Pro and the DGX Spark desktop Nvidia launched last year, the new mini PCs are Mac Mini or Mac Studio alternatives for developers working with local AI models, as well as RTX-accelerated software. That includes the AI-powered features for tools like Adobe Premiere and Photoshop, and new DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support in Blender 5.3. They can run games too , and Windows on Arm game support is improving, but at these prices, that’s not a realistic reason to pick one up yet. Nvidia says they can act as a “dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents,” and deliver “up to 1 petaflop of AI performance.” They also feature native CUDA support and access to Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux.

historyItems.originalTitle: Project Gryffindor: Meta's plan to get more school kids using Instagram
historyItems.originalSummary: Internal Meta documents show the company planned to boost Instagram use among teens by targeting schools in an initiative it named "Project Gryffindor." The project focused on growing what it called "school communities" in the U.S. by encouraging teens to include their school banner on their profiles and establishing a student directory that allows users to see and connect with others from their school who use the platform. Meta launched the initiative in 2025, calling it a "school partnership program," and significantly expanded it in September 2026. The company said almost 17,000 schools had signed up for the program at the time. Meta said the program sought to provide a safer experience on Instagram for children, including protecting them from bullying and online risks by allowing educators to report safety concerns to the company. Another feature gives school-related accounts the ability to post stories and notes visible to all verified students and parents in a school community. Meta said these features would help students and parents stay informed about happenings at school. The announcement gave an example of a school using the Instagram Stories feature to share a notice of basketball tryouts. However, in internal documents prior to the program's public launch, the company discussed more explicitly commercial motivations for establishing school networks. In a 2024 presentation on Project Gryffindor, Meta said that embedding in schools was a way to increase user "acquisition," "friending" and "invites" to join Instagram. Gryffindor is one of the four Hogwarts school houses from the Harry Potter books. "We believe network connections will fuel organic and unattributed acquisition," the project's presentation states, referring to adding new users. "Our current strategy of relying on power user teens to get less active friends onto IG may not be effective if there are full communities of teens that have not yet joined IG," the presentation stated. The previously unreported Meta documents are part of evidence obtained by lawyers through discovery in a multidistrict lawsuit alleging that social media platforms are designed to be harmful to users under 18, and that the companies knew their products carried risks they failed to disclose. Meta, alongside TikTok, Google and Snap, are defendants in the cases, which were brought by children and their families, school districts and state attorneys general.

historyItems.originalTitle: NASA to Cover 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission Space Station Departure
historyItems.originalSummary: NASA is preparing to broadcast the departure of a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft from the International Space Station (ISS). The spacecraft is set to return to Earth no earlier than Wednesday, November 18, after completing its 35th resupply mission. It will carry research samples, equipment, and other cargo back from the station. According to NASA, Dragon is scheduled to undock from the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module at 11:05 a.m. EST, depending on weather conditions. Ground controllers at SpaceX’s facility in Hawthorne, California, will send the command for the spacecraft to leave. NASA’s live coverage will begin at 10:45 a.m. EST. People can watch the event through the agency’s website and other streaming platforms. The full details are available on NASA’s live coverage page. SpaceX Dragon prepares to return to Earth After 34 days docked to the @Space_Station, the Dragon spacecraft supporting SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for @NASA is targeted to undock from the orbiting lab as soon as Wednesday, November 18 → https://t.co/tnMukzSxui https://t.co/OhkzWO1fRh — SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 17, 2026 NASA and SpaceX are watching weather conditions around the planned splashdown area off the California coast. The spacecraft is expected to reach the ocean no earlier than 1:50 a.m. EST on Thursday, November 19. This is 10:50 p.m. PST on Wednesday, November 18. The return schedule may change depending on weather conditions in the recovery area. NASA said it would share updates about the splashdown time on its space station blog. The agency will not provide a live broadcast of the splashdown. Research samples and equipment returning from space The spacecraft will be returning with many kilograms of scientific samples to help scientists on Earth and in space. A 3D printed blood vessel sample was studied to understand age-related disease of blood vessels and the heart. Frozen tumour organoids have also been treated on the station and will be returned to Earth to investigate how cancer treatments can be improved. Microbes, which have been frozen, will be returned to Earth to give scientists insight into how antibiotic resistant bacteria adapt and change in space. Finally, a lighting system which has been on the station for over 3 years will be returned. It was tested to see if it could assist astronauts to get better quality sleep and maintain good health during long missions. A mission that delivered more than 6,300 pounds of cargo A Dragon spacecraft carrying over 6,300 pounds of supplies, scientific experiments and equipment docked with the station on October 15. The craft was carried into space by a Falcon 9 rocket on October 13 from Florida as the 35th resupply mission for NASA and SpaceX. Experiments conducted on the International Space Station, which has been occupied by astronauts for over 26 years, are helping prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars.

historyItems.originalTitle: Microsoft and Salesforce Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Trusted Customer Context and Action into Microsoft AI Experiences
historyItems.originalSummary: REDMOND, Wash., and SAN FRANCISCO — Nov. 17, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce Inc. (NYSE: CRM) today announced Copilotforce, a new partnership that helps employees get more done in the tools they already use by bringing Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into Microsoft Copilot and other AI-powered productivity experiences. Unveiled at Microsoft Ignite, the partnership introduces new integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric, including Salesforce in Copilot, a plugin available in public preview with 38+ prebuilt sales skills. Together, these capabilities help businesses move faster, reduce manual work and get more value from their existing technology investments — while maintaining the security, governance and permissions they already rely on. Bringing Salesforce workflows together with conversations, meetings and documents in Microsoft 365 means less time spent moving between systems and more time on the work that matters. Salesforce in Copilot connects customer context with the work happening across the business so employees can make more informed decisions and take action without constantly switching applications. Microsoft Work IQ, the intelligence layer powering Copilot, provides relevant context from Teams meetings, Outlook emails and documents across SharePoint and OneDrive. Work IQ and Salesforce help sellers understand not only what’s recorded in CRM, but what’s happening across customer conversations and collaboration — and what needs to happen next. Through authenticated Salesforce MCP access, sellers can securely retrieve customer information and take supported business actions within their existing Salesforce permissions. Salesforce continues to govern access and business actions, while Microsoft applies its existing enterprise compliance controls to communications and documents. Data, context and the apps where sellers work come to life in practical workflows across the sales cycle, including: With Copilot as the front door to business process, Salesforce in Copilot allows organizations to bring together Salesforce data, workflows, agents and prebuilt skills from the systems they already rely on through Copilot’s open and interoperable platform. “Through Copilotforce, we’re bringing Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today, embedding trusted Salesforce context and intelligent sales workflows directly where sellers work,” said Miguel Milano, President & Chief Operating Officer, Salesforce . “By bringing together the #1 CRM with the #1 productivity surface, we’re transforming AI from a standalone tool into a powerful driver of productivity, smarter decisions and customer success.” Expanding connection in the places people work For many organizations, the work first starts in Microsoft Teams, where people share files, make decisions and hand work to each other. historyItems.originalTitle: Microsoft and Salesforce Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Trusted Customer Context and Action into Microsoft AI Experiences
historyItems.originalSummary: REDMOND, Wash., and SAN FRANCISCO — Nov. 17, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce Inc. (NYSE: CRM) today announced Copilotforce, a new partnership that helps employees get more done in the tools they already use by bringing Salesforce customer context, business processes and actions into Microsoft Copilot and other AI-powered productivity experiences. Unveiled at Microsoft Ignite, the partnership introduces new integrations across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Fabric, including Salesforce in Copilot, a plugin available in public preview with 38+ prebuilt sales skills. Together, these capabilities help businesses move faster, reduce manual work and get more value from their existing technology investments — while maintaining the security, governance and permissions they already rely on. Bringing Salesforce workflows together with conversations, meetings and documents in Microsoft 365 means less time spent moving between systems and more time on the work that matters. Salesforce in Copilot connects customer context with the work happening across the business so employees can make more informed decisions and take action without constantly switching applications. Microsoft Work IQ, the intelligence layer powering Copilot, provides relevant context from Teams meetings, Outlook emails and documents across SharePoint and OneDrive. Work IQ and Salesforce help sellers understand not only what’s recorded in CRM, but what’s happening across customer conversations and collaboration — and what needs to happen next. Through authenticated Salesforce MCP access, sellers can securely retrieve customer information and take supported business actions within their existing Salesforce permissions. Salesforce continues to govern access and business actions, while Microsoft applies its existing enterprise compliance controls to communications and documents. Data, context and the apps where sellers work come to life in practical workflows across the sales cycle, including: With Copilot as the front door to business process, Salesforce in Copilot allows organizations to bring together Salesforce data, workflows, agents and prebuilt skills from the systems they already rely on through Copilot’s open and interoperable platform. “Through Copilotforce, we’re bringing Salesforce to the largest surface in enterprise software today, embedding trusted Salesforce context and intelligent sales workflows directly where sellers work,” said Miguel Milano, President & Chief Operating Officer, Salesforce . “By bringing together the #1 CRM with the #1 productivity surface, we’re transforming AI from a standalone tool into a powerful driver of productivity, smarter decisions and customer success.” Expanding connection in the places people work For many organizations, the work first starts in Microsoft Teams, where people share files, make decisions and hand work to each other. historyItems.originalTitle: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
historyItems.originalSummary: Tesla, Inc. (NasdaqGS:TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NasdaqGS:SPCX) are reportedly advancing merger talks, with a potential December announcement. The proposed $3.5 trillion-plus deal could unite their AI, robotics, automotive and?Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX are reportedly making progress on merger discussions, with an announcement possible as early as December. The proposed combination could become one of the largest corporate transactions in history. The announcement could coincide with Tesla's December 3 annual shareholder meeting, although the timeline could extend into early 2027.(Sources: TradingView, Investors.com) Negotiations have reportedly advanced to discussions over deal structure, valuation and governance arrangements. Boards and advisers from both companies are involved in the process, with independent director committees established to evaluate a potential combination. However, no final agreement has been reached, and there is no guarantee that a deal will materialise.A merger could bring together SpaceX's estimated $1.9 trillion valuation and Tesla's market capitalisation of approximately $1.6 trillion. The combination would bring Musk's major businesses under one corporate structure and could rank among the largest mergers ever. The share-exchange ratio and ownership allocation between investors remain key issues in the negotiations.The proposed merger could combine Tesla's electric vehicle and robotics operations with SpaceX's aerospace and satellite businesses. Both companies have overlapping ambitions in artificial intelligence and advanced computing, creating potential opportunities in AI software, chip design, robotics and SpaceX's Starlink satellite network. Their Terafab semiconductor project could also play an important role in the combined company's technology ambitions.The proposed combination could face significant regulatory and operational challenges, particularly given Tesla's manufacturing operations in China and SpaceX's US government and defence contracts. National security considerations, regulatory scrutiny and shareholder approvals will be important factors in determining the deal's feasibility.

About Amkor Technology, Inc., Aehr Test Systems and Inc. Amkor Technology, Inc. provides outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services in the United States, Japan, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. It offers turnkey packaging and test services, including semiconductor wafer bump, wafer probe, wafer back-grind, package design, packaging, burn-in, system-level and final test, and drop shipment services; flip chip scale package products for smartphones, tablets, and other mobile consumer electronic devices; flip chip stacked chip scale packages that are used to stack memory digital baseband, and as applications processors in mobile devices; flip-chip ball grid array packages for various networking, storage, computing, automotive, and consumer applications; and memory products for system memory or platform data storage. In addition, it offers micro-electro-mechanical systems packages that are miniaturized mechanical and electromechanical devices; and advanced system-in-package modules used in radio frequency and front end modules, basebands, connectivity, fingerprint sensors, display and touch screen drivers, sensors and MEMS, and NAND memory and solid-state drives. Further, the company provides wafer, package, and system level test services, as well as burn-in test and test development services. It serves integrated device manufacturers, fabless semiconductor companies, original equipment manufacturers, and contract foundries. Amkor Technology, Inc. was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. JUMP TO: FIRST DAY OF WINTER l ‘SUPER EL NIÑO’ l SNOW TOTAL PREDICTIONSWinter forecasts this year come down to four key indicators: Winter officially begins in the Northern Hemisphere on Dec. 21 with the winter solstice – the day with the least amount of possible daylight and the longest night.El Niño refers to warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures along the equatorial latitude in the Pacific Ocean.It causes an intensified southern jet stream that forces the polar jet stream to retreat further into southern Canada. The results are milder, dry conditions in the northern U.S. and a cool, wetter-than-normal forecast for the southern part of the country.This year, we're experiencing a "Super El Niño," with water temperatures rising to a historic 4.77°F above average, outpacing each of the four previous "Super El Niño" years of 2015, 1997, 1982 and 1877. A strong El Niño winter doesn't automatically mean there won't be snow. It tends to bring more coastal storms along the Eastern Seaboard, but the above-average temperatures mean rain is more likely.El Niño can still cause a variety of outcomes. In 2015-2016, the region saw a total of 31.2" of snow, but 27.5" came from one blockbuster storm in January 2016.Here are the other previous totals:Gregory describes the polar vortex as a high-speed "racetrack wind pattern" that circles the North Pole when stable. If it becomes fractured or weakened, arctic air can spill down into the eastern U.S. The polar vortex weakened in early November this year, which has never happened for as long as forecasters have been tracking it. This is worth keeping an eye on. The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) is a pressure oscillation that stretches from the North Atlantic down to the subtropical Atlantic.When in its negative phase, the NAO forms a blocking pattern around Greenland that forces cold air down from Canada, resulting in coastal storms. In the past, this has caused some major snowstorms in the New York City area. In its positive phase, the NAO sees much stronger pressure variation in the Atlantic, resulting in a stronger westerly wind. Cold air stays north, keeping temperatures mild around here. Arctic, or Siberian, snow cover started early this year. In fact, it's already above average. What does that mean? Colder air can more easily travel across the North Pole, disrupt the polar vortex and send more cold air into the eastern U.S. Gregory predicts there will be multiple coastal storms this winter, but with a lower-than-average amount of snow. Since the super El Niño leads to milder temperatures, the storms can vary between snow, ice and rain along the coast. You'll probably have to be well inland to get a good amount of snow this year.Gregory predicts New York City and the nearby suburbs could see 12-20" of snow this year, but he notes that might be too generous, all things considered. historyItems.originalTitle: FAA Air Traffic Ground Stop Investigation: HPE Juniper Routers, Cisco Routers, And The Aftermath Of A Telecom Network Upgrade
historyItems.originalSummary: Here’s a look at how a telecom network upgrade involving a move from 20-year-old Cisco routers to modern HPE Juniper routers led to the nationwide air traffic ground stop last Friday. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide air traffic ground stop last Friday, which resulted from a telecom network upgrade involving a move from 20-year-old Cisco routers to modern HPE Juniper routers, is now zeroing in on older Cisco equipment, said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in an interview on CNBC. “What happened was as we did one of those switchovers in El Dorado, Ark., that server or that router started to flood our network,” said Duffy Monday of the network upgrade from old copper wires to fiber. “Well, all of the work I had done to put in new equipment, those routers in my system didn’t go down. But we also use a lot of 2001 Cisco servers that went out of commission in 2006. It is those old servers that were flooded and started to give us inconsistency in our network.” At this point, Duffy said, the Cisco server in question has been taken to federal contractor and technology solution provider L3Harris Technologies’ Florida laboratory as part of an investigation into the incident with FAA staff on site. CRN reached out to Cisco for comment but had not heard back at press time. As a result of the network issue, Duffy said the decision was made to “shut down the airspace” until the U.S. could “isolate where the flooding of the network was coming from, remedy it, get the systems working again and get air travel back to normal,” said Duffy. In a press conference on Saturday, Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters that the FAA spends a billion dollars a year maintaining and sustaining its 1980s TDMI telco network, which he referred to as a 1G system. “We are constantly replacing 2,000 Cisco 600 routers with Juniper routers,” he said. “So, this is ordinary course-of-business stuff.” Those Cisco 600 routers were manufactured between 2001 and 2006. The upgrade from Cisco routers to HPE Juniper equipment was being conducted by Melbourne, Fla.-based L3Harris, which is under contract with the U.S. government, runs the telecom network. L3Harris, which has been working with the FAA for over 20 years, is now under scrutiny on whether there was a misconfiguration issue with regard to the HPE Juniper router as part of the network upgrade.

historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk Wants to Merge Tesla and SpaceX. Their Businesses Already Overlap.
historyItems.originalSummary: Thank you for your patience while we verify access. Nearly a decade ago, Elon Musk gave Tesla’s design team an unusual assignment: Build a sports car that can fly. Mr. Musk brought in a small team of engineers from SpaceX, his rocket company, to lend a hand. Led by Bill Riley, SpaceX’s executive overseeing engineering on the rocket intended to land NASA astronauts on the moon, the team juggled their day jobs with outfitting a Roadster sports car with cold-gas thrusters, a technology more commonly found in rockets that has enough force to burst a human eardrum, according to three people familiar with the project. This year, as engineers from both companies prepared for the car’s debut, they spent months putting it through its paces at SpaceX’s rocket testing facility in McGregor, Texas, the people said. In October, a driverless Roadster did a kick flip in midair, launching off a ramp more than 60 feet high. This is “what happens when you have a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company” Mr. Musk told the crowd.

historyItems.originalTitle: Nebius Lowers Outlook, Addresses Worries Over Financing AI Buildout
historyItems.originalSummary: By Kelly Cloonan Nebius Group lowered its full-year revenue outlook, citing a delay in some third-party capacity. The artificial-intelligence cloud company also addressed recent concerns over financing its buildout, emphasizing its momentum with customer prepayments. Nebius said Thursday it now expects full-year revenue to come in at the low end of its prior guidance range of $3 billion to $3.4 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet are forecasting $3.35 billion. The updated guidance factors in a portion of this year's revenue moving into next year, with some third-party capacity Nebius had expected to come online this year now scheduled for the first half of 2027, the company said. The contracts behind that capacity remain in place, the company said. Nebius also gave an initial outlook for next year, guiding for revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, compared with analyst projections of $12.09 billion. The company said the forecast reflects a conservative approach to the pace of its buildout, and that it continues to expect to bring online more than 1 gigawatt of new capacity each year. "Our focus remains on building a healthy, profitable business for the long term," Chief Executive Arkady Volozh said in a letter to shareholders. The guidance comes amid investor worries over how neocloud companies will finance their growing footprints. CoreWeave, whose borrowing costs have surged in recent weeks and helped spark the market jitters, eased some of those concerns earlier this week after reporting better-than-expected quarterly revenue. Volozh said Nebius is able to finance its buildout in a prudent way through customer prepayments and a healthy balance sheet, helped by a strategy that lets it command premium prices and terms, and bring down its costs of infrastructure from designing and building it itself. Nebius expects prepayments and financing against existing contracts with investment-grade customers to cover 75% to 85% of its capital expenditures in 2027, and has a wide range of other funding options available, Volozh said. "Our confidence in the fundamentals of what we are building has not changed, and the opportunity ahead of us is as large as it has ever been. We will keep going," Volozh said. Nebius shares slid 12% to $136.66 in premarket trading. Nebius reported a third-quarter loss of $37.5 million, or 13 cents a share, compared with a loss of $119.6 million, or 50 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenue surged by more than six-fold to $980.8 million, compared with analyst estimates of $907.2 million. Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com (END) Dow Jones Newswires 11-12-26 0838ET

historyItems.originalTitle: Marvell and Penguin Solutions Collaborate to Address Data Center AI Memory and Accelerate Inference at Scale
historyItems.originalSummary: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL), a leader in data infrastructure semiconductor solutions and Penguin Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: PENG), the AI Factory Platform Company, today announced a strategic collaboration to address AI memory demands. This collaboration brings together two complementary technologies: CXL-based memory expansion that enables data centers to extend server memory capacity using existing DDR4 memory, and advanced photonic technology designed to enable high-bandwidth, low latency memory sharing across multiple racks.As AI workloads shift from model training to large-scale inference and agentic AI, memory capacity, bandwidth, and latency are becoming critical constraints on application performance and token economics. Growing model sizes, longer context windows, and expanding KV-cache requirements are driving memory needs into hundreds of gigabytes and increasingly terabytes per node. These demands are accelerating the shift beyond traditional server-attached memory toward memory expansion, pooling, and disaggregation technologies such as CXL and optical shared-memory fabrics, enabling memory capacity to scale independently of compute.Two Complementary Levels of Memory ExpansionMarvell and Penguin Solutions are developing two complementary memory expansion technologies designed to address AI infrastructure needs at the server and pod levels:Direct-attach memory expansion: The planned addition of Marvell® Structera™ X memory-expansion controllers within Penguin Solutions SMART® CXL AICs enables data centers to unlock additional memory capacity by recycling existing high-density DDR4 memory modules from decommissioned servers and connecting them directly to servers through PCIe 5.0 and CXL 2.0. This approach provides scalable, low-latency memory expansion in a standard form factor designed for broader industry adoption.Multi-rack photonic memory pooling: By integrating Marvell® Photonic Fabric™ optical interconnect technology-based memory modules and NICs into Penguin Solutions MemoryAI™ memory appliances and ComputeAI™ systems, AI data centers will be able to support low-latency, high-bandwidth, multi-rack disaggregated memory sharing across longer distances, enabling petabyte-scale memory pools for context-rich agentic AI inference.These two technologies are highly complementary. Direct-attach memory expansion addresses immediate, server-level capacity needs today, while multi-rack photonic memory sharing is designed to enable high-bandwidth, low-latency memory sharing across multiple racks to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. Together, these approaches are designed to provide customers with greater flexibility to expand memory capacity and scale AI infrastructure as its needs evolve, offering a single upgrade path from direct-attach expansion to disaggregated, multi-rack sharing, without re-architecting their infrastructure at each step.An additional benefit of the standard AIC form factor is its ability to support memory expansion beyond direct server attachment. historyItems.summary: SK HYNIX plans to open a semiconductor testing facility in 2027 in partnership with the South Korean government, angling to boost the global competitiveness of the country’s smaller chip equipment makers. The 874.6 billion won (US$654 million) facility is being built inside the sprawling Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, which is under construction south of Seoul, SK Hynix said in a statement on Monday (Nov 16). The Trinity Fab facility will open in May with equipment that small and medium-sized suppliers can use to conduct final performance and yield validation before their products are deployed in commercial chipmaking lines, it said.

historyItems.originalTitle: ULA suffers first outright failure with loss of Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
historyItems.originalSummary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, lifts off from Cape Canaveral's pad 41. A failure 10 minutes into flight resulted in the loss of 40 Amazon Leo satellites. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now In a major setback for United Launch Alliance, the company’s new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket carrying a batch of Amazon Leo internet satellites, malfunctioned during the climb to space Sunday, dooming the payload and throwing a costly wrench into the launch schedule of both companies. “Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 (at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station) suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit,” ULA said in a statement some 50 minutes after liftoff. “We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action and return to flight as quickly as possible.” It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006. It wasn’t immediately known what went wrong, but the Vulcan, the rocket replacing ULA’s fleet of Atlas 5 rockets, will face a potentially significant grounding while engineers review telemetry and implement fixes for whatever caused the mishap. It was only the fifth flight of a Vulcan rocket and the first in nine months as ULA and booster-supplier Northrop Grumman worked to resolve problems with nozzles used by strap-on solid-fuel boosters that marred two earlier flights. The solids appeared to work normally Sunday, helping boost the rocket out of the dense lower atmosphere before burning out and falling away. The two methane-burning BE-4 engines powering the Vulcan’s first stage then continued the climb toward orbit, but they appeared to fire longer than expected based on ULA’s pre-launch timeline. After stage separation, the Vulcan’s hydrogen-fueled Centaur upper stage engines took over for a planned 12-minute 15-second burn. According to ULA’s update, something went wrong during that Centaur firing, but no additional details were immediately provided. Sunday’s launch was the first of 38 Vulcan flights purchased by Amazon to launch its Leo satellites, designed to compete head-to-head with Elon Musk’s Starlinks and other space-based internet providers. ULA already has launched eight LEO flights using Atlas 5 rockets.

historyItems.originalTitle: Firefly Aerospace Inks $1.3 Billion Deal With AST SpaceMobile for Rocket Engines
historyItems.originalSummary: Firefly Aerospace has signed an agreement valued at more than $1.3 billion with AST SpaceMobile to supply rocket engines, license engine intellectual property, and provide engineering support for AST SpaceMobile’s new heavy-lift launch vehicle. The three-year agreement includes the delivery of 36 rocket engines and provides AST SpaceMobile with rights to manufacture engines using Firefly’s technology. The transaction represents a substantial commercial agreement for Firefly and supports AST SpaceMobile’s strategy of developing its own launch infrastructure for satellite deployments. Under the agreement, Firefly will provide 27 Miranda engines and nine Vira vacuum engines for AST SpaceMobile’s first three rockets. The engines will support development of a new heavy-lift launch vehicle intended to deploy AST SpaceMobile’s BlueBird satellites into low Earth orbit. AST SpaceMobile is developing a space-based cellular broadband network designed to provide connectivity directly to standard mobile devices. The company requires substantial launch capacity to deploy its satellite constellation and expand network coverage. Developing its own launch vehicle could provide greater control over launch schedules and reduce dependence on third-party rocket availability. Firefly will supply the propulsion technology while maintaining ownership of its underlying intellectual property. AST SpaceMobile will receive a license allowing it to manufacture the engines for its launch program.

historyItems.title: SpaceX 歷史性首次捕捉 Starship 火箭上級
historyItems.summary: SpaceX has achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme by successfully catching the rocket's upper stage using giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. The spacecraft returned to Earth after spending 22.5 hours in space, marking the first successful recovery of the Ship through this technique. However, the mission was only partially successful, as the rocket's lower section failed its planned recovery attempt. Starship completes 22.5-hour flight The 124-metre-tall Starship rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, at 16:47 local time on Friday.
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX has achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme by successfully catching the rocket's upper stage using giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. The spacecraft returned to Earth after spending 22.5 hours in space, marking the first successful recovery of the Ship through this technique. However, the mission was only partially successful, as the rocket's lower section failed its planned recovery attempt. Starship completes 22.5-hour flight The 124-metre-tall Starship rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, at 16:47 local time on Friday. This was the 15th test flight of the spacecraft and the first attempt to recover both sections of the rocket during the same mission. After reaching space, the upper stage, known as the Ship, deployed 26 satellites for SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation. It subsequently completed 14 orbits around Earth before beginning its return journey. The moment a Starship booster exploded during an attempted landing at SpaceX’s facility today. https://t.co/HoRscWHVH0 — распад и неуважение (@VictorKvert2008) November 14, 2026 &nbsp; How did SpaceX catch Starship? As the Ship approached its launch site, it hovered near the launch tower, where two enormous mechanical arms, nicknamed 'chopsticks', moved into position and secured the returning spacecraft. The arms are part of SpaceX's Mechazilla recovery system, which is designed to catch returning rocket stages instead of allowing them to land on the ground using conventional landing legs. This was the first time SpaceX successfully caught Starship's upper stage. The company had previously demonstrated the technique with its Super Heavy booster, which it had caught on three earlier test flights. What happened to Starship's booster? While the upper-stage recovery succeeded, the mission encountered a problem during the attempted recovery of the Super Heavy booster. The lower section was expected to return to the launch tower approximately six and a half minutes after liftoff. However, an automated abort system cancelled the catch attempt and diverted the booster towards the ocean. The booster hovered above the water before bursting into flames. Elon Musk later said on X that it was "slightly low on fuel". Why does SpaceX want to recover both stages? SpaceX aims to make Starship completely reusable to reduce the cost of launching payloads into space. Recovering both sections would allow the company to inspect, refuel and prepare the rocket for subsequent flights. The approach builds on the company's Falcon 9 programme, whose reusable boosters have helped reduce launch costs. Why is this important for NASA's Moon mission? Starship's development is closely linked to NASA's Artemis programme. SpaceX has a contract to develop a lunar lander based on Starship that could transport astronauts to the Moon's surface. However, the company must demonstrate reliable recovery and repeated operations before Starship can fulfil its ambitious role in future lunar missions.

However, the mission was only partially successful, as the rocket's lower section failed its planned recovery attempt. historyItems.originalSummary: The lawsuit alleges Fluence Energy's fiscal 2026 guidance rested on contract manufacturing facilities that were not ready to produce at assumed volumes. NEW YORK , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SueWallSt alerts investors in Fluence Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: FLNC ) of a pending securities class action on behalf of purchasers of Fluence Energy securities between November 24, 2025 and September 16, 2026. Find out if you may qualify to recover losses or contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. at [email protected] or (888) SueWallSt. FLNC closed at $28.99 on February 4, 2026, and faltered to just $18.95 the following day, a decline of $10.04 per share, or about 34.63%. The complaint highlights two further declines of about $1.02, or 7.17% on August 6, 2026 and of $1.39, or about 15.36% on September 17, 2026. To be considered for lead plaintiff, investors must file by November 27, 2026. The Market Impact of Each FLNC Disclosure Day As averred, the decline unfolded in stages because Fluence Energy reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 outlook alongside the February 4, 2026 results and again on May 6, 2026. The pleading asserts that the Company did not disclose that delivering backlog and recognizing guided revenue depended on new contract manufacturing facilities that were not completed, not operational, or not capable of the assumed volumes. It further asserts that corrective measures at the Company's contract manufacturers were not remediating the production problems. The complaint charges that the August 5, 2026 report, which blamed weaker revenue on "production delays at new contract manufacturing facilities," and the September 16, 2026 update, which cited "continuing supply chain issues affecting the Company's U.S. production," each partially corrected those alleged misstatements. "Fluence Energy shareholders absorbed three heavy-volume selloffs in under eight months, and the complaint alleges each one followed news about contract manufacturing problems that had not been disclosed when guidance was set. Where an outlook is reaffirmed between those declines, investors are entitled to ask what management knew about production readiness at the time." -- Joseph E. Levi, Esq. historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Benefits From Strong Test Demand: Can It Beat KLAC & COHU?
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne TER is benefiting from strong semiconductor test demand, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, and increasing complexity in advanced chip architectures. Rising demand for AI accelerators, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and high-performance computing solutions is strengthening the company's growth prospects and competitive position against KLA KLAC and Cohu COHU. Teradyne reported impressive third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues surging 70% year over year to $1.31 billion. Semiconductor Test revenues increased 77% to more than $1 billion, supported by robust demand for AI accelerators, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and power management solutions. Compute revenues grew nearly 50%, while memory revenues reached a record $301 million, reflecting strong demand for HBM and DRAM testing. Teradyne's expanding product portfolio is another key growth driver. The company's UltraFLEXplus platform is gaining traction as hyperscalers increasingly adopt dual-vendor testing strategies. Its recently introduced UltraVS64-HP, UltraPort-PCIe6 and Magnum E2 solutions strengthen its ability to address next-generation AI accelerators, high-speed connectivity and advanced memory testing requirements. Teradyne expects additional hyperscaler capacity purchases and compute-related revenue opportunities in 2027. Teradyne's expanding AI-driven opportunities and product innovations position it favorably to sustain momentum against KLAC and COHU. For the fourth quarter of 2026, Teradyne expects revenues between $1.25 billion and $1.35 billion. The midpoint of the guidance range stands at $1.30 billion.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX’s Starship Launch Today Could Lift the Stock
historyItems.originalSummary: If you find yourself in Texas during the next flight of SpaceX's massive Starship rocket , you may be in for quite a show. Anytime the world's largest rocket is due to get off the ground at SpaceX's Starbase headquarters in Boca Chica, a crowd is sure to form at the nearby South Padre Island . This time, though, it may not be just the launch of Starship that attracts spectators, but the possible return a day later of the rocket's upper section to South Texas. Up until now, SpaceX has sought to land the upper stage vehicle in distant oceans after it hits its objectives and completes its test flights. In some infamous cases, the vehicle has even accidentally exploded in the air mid-flight. For the first time, though, the plan is for both Starship's stages to travel back to Starbase after doing their jobs. And in the case of the upper stage, that dramatic landmark homecoming should take it over a large swath of Texas . Here's where you can watch SpaceX conduct its next Starship flight test from Starbase, Texas, as well as what to expect for a mission referred to as flight 15 . SpaceX, which tech mogul Elon Musk founded in 2002, is developing Starship to be a fully reusable transportation system, meaning both the rocket and vehicle can return to the ground for additional missions. Reaching 407 feet tall when fully stacked, Starship is regarded as the largest and most powerful launch vehicle ever developed. The rocket is composed of both the 236-foot lower stage booster known as Super Heavy that provides the initial burst of thrust at liftoff, and a 171-foot upper stage that flies in orbit. The third and latest prototype of Starship, known as Version 3 (V3) is still undergoing test flights as SpaceX races to have it ready for NASA's Artemis lunar landings and Musk's own dreams of crewed trips to Mars . Starship is also central to SpaceX's plans of expanding its Starlink satellite internet business. SpaceX is working toward a Friday, Nov. 13, launch of its Starship rocket, the company announced . The launch window is due to open from 4:45 to 6 p.m. CT. This time, though, spectators in Texas may want to make a point to not just catch the launch, but the return of the section of the rocket that flies in space nearly a day later (see more on that below).

historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia Federal Solutions awarded Department of War RAPID contract to advance multi-domain threat awareness
historyItems.originalSummary: CHANTILLY, Va., 13 November 2026 | 14:00 PM Europe/Amsterdam Nokia Federal Solutions awarded Department of War RAPID contract to advance multi-domain threat awareness Press Release Nokia Federal Solutions today announced that it has been awarded a contract under the Department of War's (DoW) RAPID project, managed by the FutureG Office within the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)). The award supports Real-World Application Prototyping for ISAC Demonstration (RAPID), leveraging 5G and 6G infrastructure for object detection and tracking. Under the contract, Nokia Federal will develop, build and test integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) capabilities and demonstrate an end-to-end solution for the DoW's RAPID project. The effort supports the FutureG Office's mission by demonstrating how 5G and future 6G networks can be leveraged to improve threat detection and situational awareness, helping protect critical infrastructure against emerging threats. Built on Nokia's AI-RAN platform, the project will integrate Nokia and third-party applications for sensing and spectrum threat awareness. It will combine multiple sensing modalities and sensor fusion to help provide a more comprehensive picture of potential unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) threats. Subcontractors supporting the effort include Nokia affiliates, Texas Tech University, DeepSig, Hidden Level and Future Technologies. " The unmanned system threat is real. Integrated sensing and communications provides the opportunity to help protect critical infrastructure by leveraging the existing cellular networks to identify the threat. This project in partnership with Department of War is helping to advance the technology and the ecosystem to make that a reality. Steve Vogelsang, Chief Technology Officer, Nokia Federal Solutions " " In the FutureG Office, we are accelerating and adapting commercial wireless technologies to meet the requirements of the Department of War, and ISAC is at the forefront of this effort. Through RAPID and related initiatives, we are cultivating an open ecosystem that enables us to leverage commercial cellular infrastructure to bolster force protection and defense of critical assets against evolving UAV threats. Marlan Macklin, Deputy Principal Director for FutureG in OUSW(R&E) " The award reinforces Nokia Federal's role in supporting the DoW FutureG Office's mission by bringing proven commercial innovation into mission-critical environments. It also highlights how commercial technologies can be applied to meet the DoW's most demanding operational requirements. historyItems.title: ULA 推遲週日火神火箭為亞馬遜發射 40 顆 Leo 衛星
historyItems.summary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, stands ready for launch at Cape Canaveral's pad 41. The rocket will carry 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now. Update: Launch has now slipped to Sunday at 12:11 p.m.
historyItems.originalTitle: ULA delays to Sunday Vulcan rocket launch of 40 Leo satellites for Amazon
historyItems.originalSummary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, stands ready for launch at Cape Canaveral's pad 41. The rocket will carry 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now. Update: Launch has now slipped to Sunday at 12:11 p.m. EST (1711 UTC) due to a network communication issue between the ground and the rocket that could not be resolved in time for Saturday’s launch window. United Launch Alliance will try again Saturday to launch its Vulcan rocket after a power interruption at a nitrogen plant scrubbed Friday’s attempt, further postponing the 215-foot-tall vehicle’s return to flight after solid rocket booster nozzles failed on two of its first four missions. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is now scheduled for 12:32:30 p.m. EST (1732:30 UTC) Saturday, Nov. 14. ULA said the rocket and the 40 Amazon Leo satellites it carries remain healthy. “The launch of a United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket carrying the Amazon [LV-01] mission is delayed due to a power interruption in the Air Liquide gaseous nitrogen plant which resulted in the loss of their high-pressure pumps,” ULA said in a statement Friday morning. “Without confirmation of sustained commodity flow, the team has decided to realign the launch to the back-up opportunity.” Spaceflight Now will have live coverage Saturday beginning 30 minutes prior to liftoff. ULA announced the delay at 8:41 a.m. EST, a little more than four hours before the originally scheduled Friday liftoff and after the launch team had begun loading liquid oxygen into the rocket’s Centaur 5 upper stage, according to the company’s live mission updates. Gaseous nitrogen is used to purge and pressurize systems on the rocket and launchpad. The one-day delay extends a nine-month wait since the most recent solid rocket booster malfunction prompted the U.S. government to pause its use of the non-reusable rocket for national security missions. The now-delayed mission serves a private customer, Amazon, which has tasked ULA with ferrying 40 broadband internet satellites to expand its Leo constellation. It’s the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has purchased. ULA has not said how long Saturday’s launch window will last. The rocket will fly on a northeasterly trajectory upon leaving the pad.

If all goes well, it will lift off from a pad in South Texas, circle the Earth and then land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later. historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
historyItems.originalSummary: Later today, SpaceX is planning the most ambitious test yet of its massive new rocket Starship. If all goes well, it will lift off from a pad in South Texas, circle the Earth and then land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later. The test would be a major milestone for a rocket that company founder Elon Musk says he hopes will one day carry astronauts to Mars. But experts say the rapid development of Starship could also end up stranding one of the company's biggest boosters over the years: NASA. That's because as SpaceX ramps up its new rocket, it has said it will stop flying a much smaller one called Falcon 9. Falcon 9 launches the company's Dragon capsule, which is currently the only American spacecraft capable of ferrying NASA astronauts to and from the International Space Station. "Because Dragon has become such a successful and reliable vehicle, it became the de facto way for astronauts to get to orbit," said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space, a firm that tracks the space industry. According to a NASA announcement in September, the space agency has contracted with SpaceX for three additional flights to the International Space Station. That would only allow Dragon to fly through 2028, assuming the missions were flown consecutively in six month increments and no further flights are contracted with SpaceX.

historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile presses case for developing own launch vehicle
historyItems.originalSummary: Interested in AST SpaceMobile, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better. AST SpaceMobile plans to build Blacklift , a reusable rocket designed to carry up to five BlueBird satellites, with a first launch targeted for late 2028 and capacity for as many as two launches per month. The company expects to keep using providers such as SpaceX and Blue Origin for about two more years. Developing Blacklift will require several hundred million dollars in additional capital spending next year , but the company says owning launch capability could eventually cut launch costs by 75% and improve schedule certainty. AST says it is producing six satellites per month and expects 25 satellites to enable initial beta service in the U.S. and several other markets. It also reports agreements with about 60 mobile operators covering roughly 3 billion devices.

And we saw our pipeline for high-speed AI inference increase by more than 10x in the quarter.”

historyItems.originalTitle: Building a rocket is hard. AST SpaceMobile thinks it’s “simple.”
historyItems.originalSummary: During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications company AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a “simple” rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, “the best part is no part.” Avellan emphasized that AST has already procured engines for its proposed Blacklift rocket, asserting that engine development accounts for 80 percent of a typical rocket’s development cycle. “Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines,” he said of the rocket. “So big tanks—we know how to do them. We know how to do them. We know how to do them in composite.” I am not a rocket engineer, and I am not mad at Avellan. But he sure seems to be substantially underestimating the challenge of building rockets. Avellan also has a problem. AST SpaceMobile appears to be successful in building very large satellites, Bluebirds, that are capable of providing direct-to-cell capability from an orbit about 550km above Earth. The problem is there is a commercial launch crunch, and the company is struggling to get its satellites on orbit today, and projects to do so into the future. “We’re not doing this thing because we like rockets,” he said during the presentation. “We’re not doing this thing because we want to be in the launch business. We want this because we have so much demand of our satellites, and as you have seen it, we cannot get enough launches.” The Blacklift rocket will be “simple,” he said, because it will be solely tailored to lift five Bluebird satellites into low-Earth orbit at a time. It will have 20 metric tons of lift capacity, a reusable first stage, and launch twice a month from a pad at Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia that formerly served the Antares rocket. It will have all composite tanks and three stages. And, Avellan said, it will be ready to launch in 2028. If that timeline sounds preposterous, that’s because it is. However, Avellan believes AST has a workaround: It is committed to spending $1.3 billion to acquire enough engines for the first three Blacklift launches from Firefly Aerospace, as well as a license to manufacture additional engines over time. He is basing this argument on the Miranda first stage engine, which he said is “ready to fly.” But that’s not quite true. However, Miranda has not yet completed its formal qualification campaign, much less flown on an orbital rocket. Firefly chief executive Jason Kim said this week that qualification testing remains underway. Moreover, little is known publicly about the readiness of the upper stage engine, Vira, that AST is also acquiring from Firefly for its rocket.

historyItems.originalTitle: Ondas bets big on Israel with $1b. investment over past year
historyItems.originalSummary: Ondas has invested $1 billion in Israel, Dr. Judith Hocherman-Frommer, CTO and chief engineer of Ondas Autonomous Systems, announced at the UVID DroneTech 2026 conference at Expo Tel Aviv. “Investment in Israel is becoming mission critical,” she said, adding that the US-based company has acquired 27 defense-tech companies over the past 18 months, the majority being Israeli companies. The others are from the United States or Europe."We do not only acquire companies; we invest in each one to maximize its capabilities and create opportunities for collaboration among them to solve operational challenges in real time,” she added.The acquisitions are part of Ondas' broader push to build a vertically integrated defense technology company spanning the development, manufacturing, and deployment of autonomous systems. Its portfolio includes autonomous drones, counter-UAS systems, robotic ground platforms, unmanned aircraft, and systems for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions.The company's motto, she said, is “Bots before boots,” with autonomous systems leading and clearing the way ahead of the warfighter.According to Hocherman-Frommer, threats are evolving at a pace not seen before, within months rather than years, and therefore require fast, practical responses as well as strong integration between Israel's operational innovation and global manufacturing and deployment infrastructures.The modern battlefield is creating “a democratization of low-cost threats at massive scale, asymmetric warfare, and a constant learning race that demands flexibility and rapid adaptation. At the same time, these realities are colliding with multi-year development cycles and legacy architectures on the ground."In response, the defense industry needs to change its operating model, as “the response to rapidly evolving threats can no longer rely on development programs that take years to complete, nor on expensive, standalone missiles designed to counter swarms of low-cost drones."Instead, "There must be a shift toward developing simpler and faster systems, manufacturing large quantities at high quality and affordable cost, and advancing toward autonomy, where systems operate independently while human operators provide high-level oversight."“Speed is the new strategic advantage,” she stressed.Digital BatHocherman-Frommer's comments came just days after Ondas announced that it had received a purchase order under its Digital Bat program, a next-generation tactical attack drone designed to meet what the company believes could become demand for tens of thousands of affordable autonomous strike systems. The company said the order marks a transition from development toward serial production and large-scale manufacturing. Ondas said it plans to leverage its pending acquisition of ARAN Defense, an Israeli engineering and manufacturing company, to establish dedicated production lines capable of manufacturing thousands of systems. historyItems.originalTitle: TSMC Approves Up to $1 Billion Investment Plan in Anthropic, OpenAI
historyItems.originalSummary: Android Headlines / Tech News / TSMC Backs Anthropic and OpenAI With $1 Billion Investment TSMC’s board has approved an investment plan of up to $1 billion in two AI companies, OpenAI and Anthropic. It plans to invest $500 million in Anthropic IPO and another $500 million in OpenAI’s preferred stock. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has approved an investment of $1 billion in two AI companies, OpenAI and Anthropic. The world’s largest contract chipmaker plans to invest $500 million in each company. It looks forward to expanding financial ties with two well-known names in the AI industry, especially as AI demand grows. In a recent development, TSMC’s board has approved a $500 million investment in Anthropic’s upcoming Initial Public Offering (IPO). Moreover, the top management has also cleared an investment of up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock. With this financial step, the company seeks a stake in both AI companies. Anthropic has priced its IPO at between $70 and $78 per share. The tech giant is targeting a total valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. On the other hand, the Claude developer is raising another $26 billion through a separate private placement. Multiple companies worldwide are backing the funding. The list includes Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, AMD, and Microsoft. TSMC’s investment timing is particularly noticeable because it comes amid surging demand for AI chips. It already plays an important role in the AI industry and with the following step, it wants to further strengthen its position. The company is a key supplier to Nvidia, whose graphics processors are widely used to train and run AI models. TSMC has been breaking records in terms of overall growth and revenue. For reference, it recently reported its sixth consecutive quarter of record profit last month and said demand for AI-related chips remained “extremely robust”. What’s even more surprising is that it expects its revenue to grow further by 44% in 2026. The Taiwanese company recently said that the demand is so strong that its current manufacturing capacity is falling short of fulfilling it. To address this, TSMC is investing $265 billion in manufacturing facilities in Arizona . It is also exploring projects in Texas. In a nutshell, the company is going all out on AI, whether in the form of expanding its manufacturing capacity or investing $1 billion in AI companies.

historyItems.originalTitle: Viavi Solutions, Innio, Construction Partners, Gibraltar, and Lennar shares are falling, what you need to know
historyItems.originalSummary: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after hotter-than-expected October inflation data sparked fresh concerns that persistent price pressures could prompt the Federal Reserve to deliver larger interest rate increases. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers climbed 0.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in October 2026. Meanwhile, core inflation, which measures all items excluding volatile food and energy costs, advanced 0.3 percent. The higher-than-anticipated figures dampened investor sentiment across Wall Street, as persistent price pressures suggest the central bank may need to keep borrowing costs elevated for longer than previously anticipated. Rising interest rates typically weigh on corporate valuations by increasing borrowing expenses and diminishing the present value of future earnings. As Treasury yields surged following the government data release, equities faced broad-based downward pressure, highlighting market sensitivity to persistent macroeconomic headwinds. The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Among others, the following stocks were impacted: Innio’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 39 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business. Innio is down 58.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $13.77 per share, it is trading 66.5% below its 52-week high of $41.13 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Innio’s shares at the IPO in June 2026 would now be looking at an investment worth $413.51. ALSO WORTH WATCHING: Nvidia’s Quiet Partner. historyItems.originalSummary: Ge Vernova Inc (GEV) opened down by 7.06%. The Utilities sector is down by 1.54%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Ge Vernova Inc (GEV) down 7.06%; Nextera Energy Inc (NEE) down 0.71%; Eversource Energy (ES) down 0.75%. GE Vernova experienced pronounced downward pressure during the session, driven primarily by aggressive profit-taking and multiple compression across the power generation and electrical infrastructure sectors. After an extended period of outperformance fueled by the structural narrative surrounding artificial intelligence data center power demand and global grid modernization, elevated expectations have heightened sensitivity to any friction in project execution and capital expenditure cycles. A key catalyst behind the sell-off centers on renewed scrutiny over segment profitability, particularly surrounding the wind division. Persistent challenges in offshore wind project delivery, supply chain bottlenecks, and contract restructuring risks continue to act as an overhang on consolidated margins. While the company has made meaningful progress in de-risking its legacy offshore backlog, institutional investors remain cautious regarding the potential for further margin dilution or unexpected warranty charges before the segment achieves sustainable profitability. Simultaneously, broader industry dynamics within gas power and electrification equipment point to a pause in momentum. Despite robust order backlogs and favorable pricing power for heavy-duty gas turbines and grid solutions, market participants are increasingly focused on multi-year delivery timelines and the potential for utility customers to face regulatory or interconnection delays. Any indication of a moderated conversion pace from order book to revenue recognition leaves richly valued names susceptible to rapid valuation resets. Macroeconomic conditions and institutional positioning amplified the downward move. Upward pressure on benchmark yields and shifting expectations regarding federal energy policy and clean energy incentives prompted institutional desks to trim exposure to capital-intensive, high-valuation industrial names. Quantitative strategies and portfolio rebalancing away from momentum leadership into defensive value further accelerated intraday selling volume. Looking ahead, institutional focus will center on margin expansion trajectory within Electrification, cash flow conversion in the Power segment, and clear evidence of de-risking within Wind operations. historyItems.originalTitle: Will it snow? Latest on potential nor’easter headed for Philly, NYC and DC
historyItems.originalSummary: An incoming storm is set to deliver the first snow of the season to parts of New England, though the Boston area will mainly contend with a cold, windswept rain starting Thursday. Several inches of wet snow are forecast for the highest elevations of Massachusetts and Northern New England. This system is set to eventually slide off the Mid-Atlantic coast late Thursday and develop into a nor’easter, bringing more rain, wind, and some wet snow through Friday. But unlike the other nor’easters we’ve seen this fall, we should avoid major impacts like coastal flooding. This one is more of an inconvenience for Greater Boston and Southern New England. • Snow — This storm holds a decent shot of delivering a coating to a couple of inches of snow along Route 2, west of I-495, and a coating to 3 inches of wet snow in a few higher-elevation spots across the Berkshires, northern Worcester County, and most of Vermont, New Hampshire, and Maine, with isolated spots seeing 3 to 6 inches across the highest terrain. • Rain — For the lower elevations and by the coast, it just won’t be that cold for widespread snow. Greater Boston should end up with about a half inch of cold, windswept rain, a lot less than what we experienced last week . The same rain scenario plays out as you head south to Cape Cod, the South Coast, and Rhode Island.

historyItems.originalTitle: Kratos and Seagate Space Partner to Advance Mobile Offshore Launch Capabilities for National Security Missions
historyItems.originalSummary: A photo accompanying this announcement is available at https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/6bce8d6c-8a04-4d2e-bad7-c7d636371732 SAN DIEGO, Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, today announced a long-term agreement with Seagate Space for use of the company’s initial Gateway ™ offshore launch platform. The agreement supports Kratos’ planned first mission from the platform in 2027, with multiple additional launches anticipated in subsequent years. The partnership aligns Kratos’ mission of being first to market and proven record of delivering real, mission-relevant products and systems, including hypersonic test and other vehicles, rocket systems, propulsion technologies, target vehicles, and launch services, with Seagate Space’s modular, mobile offshore platform infrastructure. The Gateway series vessels are designed to provide flexible sea-based platforms to complement traditional land-based launch sites and test ranges. The announcement coincides with Seagate Space’s execution of its first Gateway platform construction contract, advancing into physical construction and toward future operational readiness.

historyItems.originalTitle: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
historyItems.originalSummary: The artificial intelligence semiconductor giant Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, after he acknowledged a romantic relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le — who is suspected of spying for the Chinese government. The tech mogul is not only one of the most powerful business leaders in the United States and the artificial intelligence sector; he also maintains a close relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump, who said Sunday that Huang is an “honorable guy” and should remain in his position. The executive, who will continue to lead the company — at least for the time being — sent a message to the tech giant’s employees on Sunday after U.S. media outlets published new details about the romantic relationship. In it, he admitted to being unfaithful to his wife. “I owe my family and all of you an apology... There is no excuse for what I did,” he wrote. “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” The explosive situation began to come to light last month, when The New York Times broke the story about suspicions that Jensen Huang may have been the target of a Chinese espionage operation through his relationship with Huang Le. U.S. officials had concluded last year — as reported by the Times and later by other outlets — that Alice Huang, then a senior executive at Megaspeed International, had shared information with the Chinese government while collaborating with Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, on the construction of data centers in Asia. U.S. investigators had launched their probe amid suspicions that Megaspeed helped Beijing gain access to advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors, the shipment of which to China is prohibited. The Singapore-based company had purchased enormous quantities of these chips from Nvidia: $4.8 billion worth over the past two years. Alice Huang was responsible for these purchasing operations at Megaspeed. Her biography indicates that she worked in China as a television journalist before becoming an executive at the Singapore-based company. According to the Times, last spring Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified memorandum detailing intelligence that showed Alice Huang had been recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security to lure Jensen Huang into a trap. That document circulated shortly before Trump’s visit to China in May. The tech company’s board of directors stated in a press release that it has no reason to believe that the company’s secrets or U.S. national security have been compromised. “Today’s news will not slow Nvidia,” said a spokesperson for the tech giant. “Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.” In its statement, the board of directors specifies that an independent committee, which will be supported by “outside independent counsel,” will conduct the investigation. historyItems.originalTitle: When will it snow in New York? Latest forecast shows late-week storm potential
historyItems.originalSummary: New Yorkers could get a more noticeable taste of winter late this week as colder air spreads into the state and a developing storm potentially brings rain and snow. The latest forecasts do not support calling this a major statewide snowstorm. However, the National Weather Service is now monitoring a late-week system that could produce measurable snow in higher elevations of central and eastern New York. Lower elevations and coastal communities are more likely to receive rain, although the forecast remains uncertain. Before that system arrives, much of the state will experience seasonable to relatively mild weather. Scattered rain showers will affect parts of upstate New York through Monday, followed by a period of quieter weather in many areas. Some snow could reach parts of New York late this week, but it is too early to determine where it will accumulate or whether the storm will become disruptive. The National Weather Service in Binghamton said a clipper-type system could move into the Ohio Valley Wednesday and Thursday before potentially helping form a coastal storm by Friday. The forecast includes chances for rain and snow Thursday and Friday, with some rain and snow showers potentially lingering into Saturday. Higher elevations would have the best chance of seeing measurable snow if the storm tracks south of the region, allowing colder air to become established. The Catskills and higher terrain of central New York are among the areas to watch. Uncertainty remains high because forecast models differ on the storm's track. Even relatively small changes could determine whether a location receives snow, a rain-snow mix or primarily rain. The National Weather Service's winter weather forecasts provide snowfall projections extending out to 72 hours, including expected accumulation and lower- and higher-end possibilities. Western New York will remain unsettled into Monday, but the precipitation is initially expected to fall as rain.

historyItems.originalTitle: Zeta Global Holdings Corp. (ZETA) latest stock news and headlines
historyItems.originalSummary: Revenue: $493 million in Q3 2026, up 46% year-over-year (30% excluding Marigold and political candidate revenue); $22 million above guidance midpoint. Adjusted EBITDA: $121 million, up 55% year-over-year; margin of 24.6%, up 140 basis points; $5.5 million above guidance midpoint. Free Cash Flow: $82 million, up 73% year-over-year; margin of 16.5%, up 260 basis points; conversion at 67.3%, up 700 basis points. Operating Cash Flow: $91 million, up 58% year-over-year. GAAP Net Income: $38 million, or $0.14 diluted EPS, versus a $0.02 loss in the year-ago period; year-to-date diluted GAAP EPS positive at $0.13. Non-GAAP EPS: $0.38 diluted, up 58% year-over-year from $0.24. Cost of Revenue (ex-D&A): 39.7% of revenue, down 120 basis points quarter-over-quarter, up 20 basis points year-over-year. Operating Expenses (ex-SBC): R&D 6.1%, G&A 12.3%, sales and marketing 17.3% of revenue, improving 5, 20, and 140 basis points year-over-year, respectively. Super-Scaled Customers: 212, up 18% year-over-year; quarterly ARPU of $2 million, up 22% year-over-year. Athena Adoption: Over 50% of super-scaled customers were monthly active Athena users (up from just over 40%); Athena adopters accounted for over 70% of revenue; top 25 Athena users grew revenue more than 70%.
